back: Combining compatible control methods, guided by scouting, to keep pests below the economic threshold with least use of chemicals.
Pest level at which the cost of control is less than the value of crop saved; act above it.
Rotation, timely planting, field hygiene and closed seasons, trap crops, push-pull, deep ploughing, healthy crops.
Predators (ladybirds), parasitoid wasps, disease organisms (Bt). Safe, no residues, but slow and killed by broad-spectrum sprays.
Pheromone traps (monitoring, mating disruption), resistant and Bt varieties, sterile insect technique.
Contact: kills on touch, must cover the pest. Systemic: absorbed and carried in sap; good for sucking pests.
Stomach poison: eaten with leaves or bait, for chewing pests. Fumigant: toxic gas in sealed stores, kills stages inside grain.
Cost, poisoning, residues, pollution, resistance, death of natural enemies and secondary pest outbreaks.
Net gain = value of crop saved − cost of control. Spray only if positive.
